modules.title: Introduction to Differential Equations (Introductory)
modules.html:
Forming and solving first-order differential equations. This section covers introduction to differential equations (introductory).

Key points

  • Find the equations of the asymptotes of the hyperbola $$\frac{x^2}{9} - \frac{y^2}{16} = 1$$. — $$y = \pm \frac{4}{3}x$$.
  • Determine the order of the differential equation $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 3\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^4 - y = 0$$. — $$2$$.

Worked examples

Q: Find the equations of the asymptotes of the hyperbola $$\frac{x^2}{9} - \frac{y^2}{16} = 1$$.
A: $$y = \pm \frac{4}{3}x$$ — Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: $$y = \pm \frac{4}{3}x$$.

Q: Determine the order of the differential equation $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 3\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^4 - y = 0$$.
A: $$2$$ — Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: $$2$$.
